note: Planning assumptions for the 3-year ROI model. Illustrative figures, not an AWS quote. Prices were read from the AWS Price List API on 2026-10-07; the other figures are judgement calls and say how to validate them.

aws_cost_per_server_year_usd.unit: USD per AWS server-equivalent per year (one m7i.xlarge: 4 vCPU, 16 GiB)
aws_cost_per_server_year_usd.rationale: A typical on-prem server is modelled as one 4 vCPU / 16 GiB general-purpose instance, bought on a 1-year standard Reserved Instance with no upfront payment, which is how a steady production workload is usually purchased. On-demand would be $1,766 a year and would lower the ROI. Compute only: storage is priced separately, and support and data transfer sit in the retained-cost assumption.
aws_cost_per_server_year_usd.source: AWS Price List API, AmazonEC2, us-east-1, Linux, shared tenancy, m7i.xlarge: $0.13336 per hour reserved (1 year, standard, no upfront) x 8,760 hours; retrieved 2026-10-07.

rightsizing_factor.unit: Fraction of the on-prem server count needed on AWS (0 to 1)
rightsizing_factor.rationale: Assumes AWS needs 70% as many servers as on-prem. On-prem fleets are usually sized for peak load plus headroom and run under-utilised, while AWS capacity can be matched to measured use and scaled. This is a judgement call, not a quote: 1.0 would mean no right-sizing benefit at all.
rightsizing_factor.source: Planning assumption (judgement). Validate with the customer's real CPU and memory utilisation data before presenting.

aws_cost_per_tb_year_usd.unit: USD per TB of data stored per year (blended block and object storage)
aws_cost_per_tb_year_usd.rationale: Assumes half the data sits on block storage (EBS gp3) and half in object storage (S3 Standard): ($960 + $276) / 2 = $618 per TB-year, rounded to $620. Data at rest only; requests, retrieval and snapshots are not modelled. Archive tiers would be cheaper for cold data such as a media archive.
aws_cost_per_tb_year_usd.source: AWS Price List API, us-east-1: EBS gp3 $0.08 per GB-month; S3 Standard $0.023 per GB-month (first 50 TB tier); retrieved 2026-10-07.

migration_cost_per_server_usd.rationale: One-off cost to assess, move, test and cut over each server: roughly 40 to 50 engineer-hours at about $75 an hour, plus migration tooling and a period of running both environments. Charged entirely in year 1. Depends heavily on how complicated the estate is.
migration_cost_per_server_usd.source: Planning assumption (judgement). Validate against a migration partner quote or an assessment of the customer's estate.

retained_cost_fraction.unit: Fraction of the current on-prem bill that remains after migration (0 to 1)
retained_cost_fraction.rationale: Assumes 40% of today's all-in infrastructure bill does not disappear: the staff who still run and secure workloads, software licences, network links, and AWS-side costs the model does not itemise such as support and data transfer. Without this the model compares a full on-prem bill with bare AWS compute and overstates the savings.
retained_cost_fraction.source: Planning assumption (judgement). Validate by splitting the customer's on-prem bill into hardware, facilities, staff, licences and network.
